targets.expr: sum by (pod) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total{pod=~"${netpod:regex}",container="dingo"}[24h]) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"}))

panels.description: One row per Dingo. **Healthy: every row up, Tip lag green, Arrival p50 under 1 s, 10 or more hot peers.** **Tip lag**: slots behind the wall clock (blue over 600 = syncing; now${syncing:csv}). **Arrival p50**: median time from a block's slot to the first copy of its header reaching this node over 6 h (`dingo_chainsync_header_arrival_delay_seconds`) - the pack's own block-propagation measure; pack-wide it is ${arrival_p50} ms. A syncing node hears no current blocks, so the column reads *syncing* for it. **Role** is producer for nodes that load forging credentials (now${producers:csv}). **Node disk** is the host filesystem, since local-path volumes report it. CPU is cores. **Next slot**: time until a producer's next scheduled leader slot (`dingo_leader_next_slot`, 1 s slots), *none scheduled* when the schedules it holds contain no further slot; the column appears once a producer runs a newer Dingo, and Forging Health has the schedule behind it.
panels.title: Dingo Health

panels.description: One lane per Dingo, grouped by network, for the last hour before the end of the time range. Each bar is one block at its slot time; height is the delay after the slot (linear to 1 s, log above; the dashed line is 1 s). Grey is the wait for the first copy of the header, colour is header to ledger adoption as the new tip. On a network with more than one Dingo, a yellow dot marks the Dingo that heard that block first, and the right-hand gutter gives each Dingo's share of firsts and its median lag when it was not first. Hover a bar for the numbers and the same block on its sibling Dingos. A syncing node (now:${syncing:csv}) gets a blue labelled lane instead of bars, so it does not read as slow. **Healthy: short green bars, no gaps, firsts shared between siblings.** Built from the `dingo_chainsync_recent_header_*` and `dingo_ledger_recent_adoption_*` rings (16 blocks per node, sampled every scrape).

panels.title: Block Lanes: Every Dingo

panels.description: One row per Dingo. **Healthy: every row up, Tip lag green, Arrival p50 under 1 s, 10 or more hot peers.** **Tip lag**: slots behind the wall clock (blue over 600 = syncing; now${syncing:csv}). **Arrival p50**: median time from a block's slot to the first copy of its header reaching this node over 6 h (`dingo_chainsync_header_arrival_delay_seconds`) - the pack's own block-propagation measure; pack-wide it is ${arrival_p50} ms. A syncing node hears no current blocks, so the column reads *syncing* for it. **Role** is producer for nodes that load forging credentials (now${producers:csv}). **Node disk** is the host filesystem, since local-path volumes report it. CPU is cores. **Next slot**: time until a producer's next scheduled leader slot (`dingo_leader_next_slot`, 1 s slots), *none scheduled* when the schedules it holds contain no further slot; the column appears once a producer runs a newer Dingo, and Forging Health has the schedule behind it.
panels.title: Dingo Resources

panels.description: One row per Dingo, one cell per time bucket (30 min or more), coloured by the worst state the node was in during that bucket. In order of severity: **down** (not scraped), **pipeline stuck** (ledger pipeline stuck or halted), **syncing** (over 600 slots behind; blue, not red, because a bootstrap is expected to take a while - now:${syncing:csv}), **lagging** (300 to 600 slots behind), **thin on peers** (under 5 hot peers), **healthy**. A gap means the target did not exist. **Healthy: a solid green grid.** A column of the same colour across nodes points at the cluster or the network; one bad row points at that node.

targets.expr: min_over_time(((max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"}) == 0) or (max by (pod) (dingo_ledger_pipeline_stuck{cardano_network=~"$network"} + dingo_ledger_pipeline_halted{cardano_network=~"$network"}) > 0) * 0 + 1 or (max by (pod) (dingo_tip_gap_slots{cardano_network=~"$network"}) > 600) * 0 + 2 or (max by (pod) (dingo_tip_gap_slots{cardano_network=~"$network"}) > 300) * 0 + 3 or (max by (pod) (cardano_node_metrics_peerSelection_hot{cardano_network=~"$network"}) < 5) * 0 + 4 or max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"}) * 0 + 5)[$__interval:1m])

panels.title: Health Grid: Dingo by Time

panels.description: One row per Dingo and version, coloured by how long the process had been running at that moment. Every amber block is a restart (the process was under 30 minutes old); it fades to green after 6 hours. A row that ends while a new row for the same Dingo starts is a version change, so a rollout reads as a staircase across the pack. Running now:${versions:csv}. **Healthy: long green bars**; amber blocks that repeat on one row are a crash loop.

targets.expr: (max by (pod, ver) (label_replace(dingo_build_info{cardano_network=~"$network"}, "ver", "$1", "version", "(v[^ ]+).*") * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (time() - process_start_time_seconds{cardano_network=~"$network"})) >= bool 1800) + (max by (pod, ver) (label_replace(dingo_build_info{cardano_network=~"$network"}, "ver", "$1", "version", "(v[^ ]+).*") * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (time() - process_start_time_seconds{cardano_network=~"$network"})) >= bool 21600)

panels.title: Restarts and Versions

panels.description: Three medians per Dingo over the dashboard time range, each measured from the block's slot: **header heard** (first copy of the header, `dingo_chainsync_header_arrival_delay_seconds`), **body fetched** (`dingo_blockfetch_block_delay_seconds`) and **adopted as tip** (`dingo_ledger_block_adoption_delay_seconds`, including validation). Sorted by header heard, fastest first, so the top row is the Dingo that hears blocks soonest. Compare Dingos on the same network; different networks have different producers and block sizes. Syncing nodes record none of these and are absent (now:${syncing:csv}), as is a Dingo that no longer exists. **Healthy: every bar under 1 s**, with adoption close behind the fetch.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, pod) (increase(dingo_chainsync_header_arrival_delay_seconds_bucket{cardano_network=~"$network"}[$__range]))) > 0) and on (pod) max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"})

(histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, pod) (increase(dingo_blockfetch_block_delay_seconds_bucket{cardano_network=~"$network"}[$__range]))) > 0) and on (pod) max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"})

(histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, pod) (increase(dingo_ledger_block_adoption_delay_seconds_bucket{cardano_network=~"$network"}[$__range]))) > 0) and on (pod) max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"})

panels.title: Slot to Tip: Leaderboard

panels.description: Every block header the pack heard, as a heatmap: time runs left to right, the delay from the block's slot to the first copy of its header bottom to top (`dingo_chainsync_header_arrival_delay_seconds` buckets, all Dingos together), and a darker cell means more headers landed in that delay bucket in that 10-minute step. Over a day it shows the hours when blocks arrive late. **Healthy: one dark band in the 0.1 to 0.5 s rows and almost nothing above 1 s** (pack median now: ${arrival_p50} ms). A band that lifts for a while at the same hours every day is network congestion at those hours; a smear above 3 s at one moment is a slow producer or a short fork, and the per-Dingo p95 below says whether one node or all of them saw it.
panels.title: Block Arrival Delay: When Are Blocks Late?

panels.description: 95th percentile delay from a block's slot to the first copy of its header reaching each Dingo, over 30-minute windows: the slow blocks, per node. The medians are on the leaderboard above and the whole distribution in the heatmap. A rise on one node points at its peers or its link; a rise on every node points at the network or at whoever produced the blocks. The shaded bands start at 2 s (amber) and 5 s (red). **Healthy: every line under the amber band.**
panels.title: Block Arrival p95 by Dingo

panels.description: Slots between the wall clock and each Dingo's chain tip, log scale so a syncing node and the at-tip nodes fit on one chart. At tip is a few slots to a few tens; over 600 (the red line) counts as syncing (now:${syncing:csv}). **Healthy: every line far below the red line.** A node at tip whose line climbs has stopped following the chain.
panels.title: Tip Lag by Dingo

panels.description: The hot (active) peers of each Dingo right now, stacked by how the node found them (`dingo_metrics_peerSelection_peers_by_source`): **ledger** peers are stake pool relays taken from the chain, **gossip** peers come from peer sharing, **local roots** are the peers pinned in the topology (for a producer, its own relays), **public roots and bootstrap** come from the topology's public lists, and the last group is inbound or unclassified. The whole bar is the node's hot peer count. **Healthy: at least 5 hot peers per Dingo (the header warns below that), relays with a healthy mix of ledger and gossip peers, producers on their local roots.** A relay whose bar is only local roots has stopped discovering peers; a short bar hears blocks late.
panels.title: Hot Peers by Source

panels.description: A fuel gauge per producer: days of KES validity left on its operational certificate (remaining KES periods times the period length, `cardano_node_metrics_remainingKESPeriods_int` x `dingo_forge_slots_per_kes_period`, 1 s slots, so 1.5 days a period). Emptiest first; a dial is full at 93 days (62 periods, a fresh key). Lowest now: ${kes_min} periods on ${kes_min_pod}. With rotation.mode Auto the operator renews at 8 periods (12 days). **Healthy: green, 12 days or more**; amber under 12 days means a rotation is due, red under 6 that it is overdue and the producer stops forging when the dial is empty.
panels.title: KES Fuel per Producer

panels.description: Days until each Dingo data volume (`dingo-data-<pod>`) is full, at the last 24 hours' fill rate (available bytes divided by the `deriv` of `kubelet_volume_stats_available_bytes`; volumes that share one filesystem report the same figure and move together). Shortest now: ${runway_min} days on ${runway_pod}. A sync or Mithril bootstrap fills fast and then stops, so a short bar while a node is syncing (now:${syncing:csv}) is a prompt to check, not a countdown. Capped at one year, which is also shown when nothing is filling. **Healthy: 30 days or more**; under 7 days act now.
panels.title: Disk Runway by Volume

panels.description: How much each Dingo's own database grew per day over the last 24 hours, summed over its stores (dingo_database_size_bytes). Negative means compaction freed more than new blocks added. Volume stats are not used here: on local-path storage every volume on a node reports that node's whole disk. **Healthy: a few MB a day at tip; a syncing Dingo grows fastest.**
panels.title: Database Growth by Dingo (per day)

panels.description: Working-set memory of each Dingo container (cAdvisor). **Healthy: flat between restarts.** Watch for steady growth on one node: that is a leak, and it ends in an OOM kill, which shows as an amber block in Restarts and Versions.

targets.expr: max by (pod) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{pod=~"${netpod:regex}",container="dingo"} * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"}))

panels.title: Memory by Dingo

panels.description: CPU each Dingo container uses, in cores (cAdvisor). Syncing and epoch boundaries spike. **Healthy: a node at tip sits low, well under one core.** A node at tip that stays high is replaying, stuck in a loop, or being hammered by a peer.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{pod=~"${netpod:regex}",container="dingo"}[5m]) * on (pod) group_left () max by (pod) (up{cardano_network=~"$network"}))

panels.title: CPU by Dingo (cores)

panels.description: On-disk size of each Dingo's database now, largest first, split into its two stores (`dingo_database_size_bytes`): the **blob store** holds the blocks, the **metadata** database the ledger state and indexes. This is what each node takes from its data volume, so read it with Disk Runway above when a volume is filling. Mainnet is far larger than the test networks. **Healthy: sizes that match the network the node follows**; two Dingos on the same network should be close, and one that is much larger than its sibling is carrying data it could shed.
panels.title: Database Size by Dingo
